title.narrative: Developing AI-enabled approaches to strengthen information integrity in Eastern Europe and Central Asia

description.narrative: This programme development phase (June – December 2026) builds on the first cohort of the FT Hub's Information Integrity Portfolio, which tested AI-enabled counter-FIMI interventions with civil society organisations in Lithuania, Moldova, and Bulgaria (January–April 2026). It is delivered by the Frontier Tech Hub (R4D).Context and rationale: The information environment in EECA is changing rapidly, with AI amplifying both threats and response capabilities. Expert interviews (FT Hub, November 2025–March 2026) identified three structural barriers: weak cooperation along the counter-FIMI response chain; limited capacity to move quickly from signal to action; and dependency on grant funding that does not build durable capability. This phase generates the strategic evidence and programme design needed to move to a well-designed, future-proofed programme.The phase has four core objectives: (1) design and launch a second cohort of AI-enabled pilots across EECA; (2) deliver two horizon scanning workshops for FCDO colleagues on the future of AI and information integrity in EECA and (3) develop a programme concept note and strategic design for a proposed ~£3m programme commencing approximately September 2026.Primary beneficiaries are FCDO/EECAD as strategic decision-maker, and civil society and other organisations across EECA. The UK's recognised leadership in countering disinformation positions FCDO to shape next-generation AI-enabled information integrity programming in the region.Key risks include delayed confirmation of FT Hub non-ODA co-funding and geopolitical events disrupting stakeholder engagement; both are mitigated through the bridge funding model and a flexible, virtual-ready delivery approach.
